Addis Ababa, "new flower" in Amharic, is the capital of Ethiopia, founded in 1886 by Emperor Menelik II and his wife Taytu near hot springs in the highlands, at about 2,350 metres. It is also a capital for Africa as a whole, as home of the African Union.

The city grew as the capital of Menelik's enlarged empire. A railway from the French port of Djibouti reached it in 1917, linking Ethiopia to the sea. Italian troops held it from 1936 to 1941 during the Italian occupation.

Under Haile Selassie it became a diplomatic centre: the Organisation of African Unity was founded there in 1963 and the UN Economic Commission for Africa sits there. Ethiopian Airlines made it an air hub. The Derg military government ruled from it from 1974 to 1991, and in May 1991, as rebels closed in, Israel flew some 14,000 Ethiopian Jews out of the city in Operation Solomon. A new electric railway to Djibouti opened in 2016.
